title: Navigator Lattice: Contextual Navigation Layers & Workspace Fastpaths
creator: Jules Nguyen
description: Problem: The current Redwood Console navigation mixes global workspace switching, per-workspace routing, and per-route cost/dashboards in ways that create discoverability issues for power users and confusion for new signups. This ticket captures a design exploration and prototype for a layered navigation approach ("Navigator Lattice") that surfaces contextual fastpaths for high-value tasks (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) while preserving a lightweight global rail for cross-workspace actions. Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-dashboard for common queries (cost by model, recent rollouts, SLO alerts). 2) Make workspace switching frictionless but intentionally visible for multi-tenant workflows. 3) Keep left-rail compact at small sizes while allowing transient contextual layers that show task-specific actions without full route switches.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype A (compact rail + transient contextual layer) usability test median task completion <= 30s for 'open model cost by route'
Design spec with annotated component states, accessible keyboard flows, and responsive rules documented in Confluence
Handoff package (Figma + tokens + interaction specs) delivered to ENG-4120 and initial implementation spike planned
Rollout UX: A/B toggles and telemetry hooks defined so PM can run a controlled launch and measure success metrics
design_notes: Explored three variants: (1) Compact rail + slide-over contextual layer, (2) Split rail with persistent quick-workspace chips, (3) Hybrid command-palette-first fastpath. Variant (1) favored for lower visual noise.
Cost lens card is surfaced in the contextual layer when a model or route is focused. Card shows 24h cost, token rate, and a 'drill into full cost dashboard' control.
Workspace fastpaths implemented as ephemeral chips pinned to top of contextual layer; switching preserves active route where possible through route pinning.
Accessibility: ensured all contextual triggers are focusable via keyboard; ARIA live regions announced when layers open/close to avoid context loss.
Mobile: the contextual layer collapses into a bottom sheet; workspace switcher becomes an inline dropdown to reduce navigation hops.
Trade-offs: More transient layers increases interaction complexity for some users but reduces deep navigation for common tasks. Need to instrument to validate.
Telemetry hooks proposed: nav.open, nav.layer.opened, nav.fastpath.used, workspace.switch.duration, costdrill.clicks
decisions: Adopt Variant (1) Compact rail + transient contextual layer as the primary pattern for the March experiment
Expose a lightweight inline workspace chip for power users; default off for new workspaces (opt-in) to avoid overwhelming new users
Keep primary left rail to 72px collapsed width with icons-only and 240px expanded width; contextual layer floats from the right of the rail rather than overlaying main content to reduce layout shift
Delay implementing the split-rail persistent approach until after metrics from the initial experiment are collected
